corrections: Traversal stack described as binary-heap memory → heap-allocated list storage; allocation heaps and priority-queue heaps stay distinct in the compiled dictionary.
Three quizzes defined h as tree height despite using h as a Python heap list → correct list meaning, with separate keeper and node counts.
AVL insert called a double rotation one rotation → one repair step comprising one or two rotations; original numerical answer keys preserved.
Top-k total work presented as actual sift levels → explicitly a worst-case growth scale, since many stream items require only a root comparison.

Top-50 Python replacement example implied exactly five-swap repair and 500 million actual Python swaps → distinguish simple downward-swap model from heapq’s implementation and arrival-dependent replacements.
d-ary heap cache and push speed declared guaranteed → fewer possible levels with workload-dependent actual performance.
Standalone height vocabulary referred to a missing diagram above → explicit earlier A–H prerequisite; exact deepest empty-child frame now also stated locally.

Red-black invariant unit mentioned uncle cases before teaching insertion → local black-height takeaway and standalone invariant title.
Trie API examples omitted required root arguments → executable signatures match table calls.
Empty radix-tree root violated unqualified twice-key-count bound → require at least one stored key and document empty-root exception.
Binary lifting climb example allowed 100,000 edges in a 100,000-node tree → at most 99,999; quiz explicitly defines n and treats 34 as table-level work rather than exact primitive jumps.
C++ associative-container costs overgeneralised → iterator erasure amortised constant; multi-key erasure includes matching-element count, while unique-key operations remain logarithmic.
Eight-byte child pointers described as universal on 64-bit machines → explicit assumed eight-byte representation; bytes, decimal MB and KiB kept distinct.
Bare no cycles alias opened Cycle → remove opposite-meaning alias.
Key-length complexity entry captured O(L log n) and O(L + k) with a linear-key-only definition → remove the mismatched aliases.
Suffix trie incorrectly aliased compressed Suffix tree → separate precise uncompressed Suffix trie entry; quadratic-space caveat and existing compressed-tree entry preserved.
Merkle Patricia definition claimed every node is referenced by its hash → Ethereum hashes longer encoded children and embeds short ones.
DOM definition implied only nested element children → also text/comment nodes; directory-tree examples qualify filesystem links.
Git DAG example implied all merge commits have two parents and unsourced popularity superlative → two or more merge parents; neutral distributed-version-control definition.
Implicit-array and iterator glossary guarantees omitted storage and one-call qualifications → contiguous slots versus referenced payloads, height-plus-one initialisation/advance scope.
Heap helper definition described max functions as removing the minimum → max counterparts reverse priority order; practical speed qualification.
Go heap.Interface omitted its sort.Interface inheritance → exact Len/Less/Swap plus Push/Pop structure.

corrections: tree-null-serialisation: the author's analogy edit had absorbed two visible facts ('Level-order with nulls … works too'; JSON/Protocol Buffers schemas) into the collapsed 'Where it stops' paragraph → restored as visible prose before the analogy.

tree-red-black-invariants analogy: 'no route … can be more than about twice as long as the shortest one' implied distance → the red-black bound is on node counts: 'twice as many stops as the route with the fewest'; mapping line now 'how many more nodes one path can have'.

tree-morris-threads analogy: the arrow was chalked on arrival at a dead end, but Morris creates the thread from the current node before descending and removes it on the return visit → arrow placed at the passage's last dead end (the in-order predecessor) before entering, rubbed out on return; mapping names the junction as the current node.

tree-binary-counts analogy limit: 'every round happens for everyone at once' was not the real difference (rounds also equal height) → the phone tree must reach everyone, a lookup follows one path; real calls are sequential.

tree-heap-order-layout analogy: 'a junior officer in one unit may outrank a senior one elsewhere' was self-contradictory → 'someone low down in one unit may hold a higher rank than someone near the top of another'.
tree-heap-merging analogy: 'each step costs only about ten comparisons' with 1,000 piles undercounts (a pop compares two children per level) → 'walks only about ten levels of the heap'.
tree-lca-single-query analogy limit: said the general-tree algorithm works by 'checking both routes upward' → it searches down from the root; reworded.
tree-lca-preprocessing reference card: the visible In words line relied on the hidden symbol k (2^k) → standalone wording (each stored jump is two half-size jumps from the previous level).

analogyReview.scope: Fresh reread of all 35 active lessons: 22 added analogy callouts checked for mapping and stated limits against the cited sources, with required facts outside the disclosure (one author slip fixed); 13 lessons recorded as not needing one, each with a reason.

tree-structure-edges.rationale: Org chart: root = chief executive, edge = reporting line, leaves = staff without reports; 250 people → 249 lines. Limit (dotted-line second manager breaks the tree; no job titles) correct. Facts stay outside.

tree-depth-height.rationale: Family generations: depth = generations below the founder, height = generations of descendants. Limit (two-parent ancestry; generation-1 numbering is node counting) correct after 'often' hedge.

tree-binary-counts.rationale: Phone tree: two calls each = logarithmic height, one call each = chain. Verifier rewrote the limit: a phone tree reaches everyone, a lookup follows one path; calls are sequential.

tree-shape-definitions.rationale: Usher filling rows left to right = complete tree; sold-out = perfect. Limit (doubling rows, parent above, nothing about 'full') correct.

tree-memory-layouts.rationale: Numbered estate plots = index arithmetic with no pointers; an empty plot keeps its number. Limit (no insertion in the middle) correct.

tree-recursive-orders.rationale: Report outline: TOC = pre-order, page totals = post-order. Limit (in-order only for binary trees; traversal is a choice) correct.

tree-iterative-orders.rationale: Code translation of recursion into an explicit stack; tracing is the objective and LIFO analogies already exist in dsa/02.

tree-level-order-queues.rationale: Searching street by street = BFS with a FIFO list and early stop. Limit (list grows on bushy trees; DFS memory) correct; 'first match' reworded to avoid a firewall link.

tree-morris-threads.rationale: Chalk arrows: verifier corrected the sequence so the arrow is placed at the passage's last dead end (in-order predecessor) before entering and rubbed out on return. Limit (visible to others; leaving early leaves cycles) correct.

tree-bst-search-insert.rationale: Higher-or-lower game = BST search path. Limit (guesses fixed by insertion order; chain needs n guesses) correct.

tree-bst-deletion-cases.rationale: Three-case procedure with before/after diagrams; a comparison would not add understanding.

tree-bst-successor-validation.rationale: The 10/5/15/6 counterexample and executable code carry the local-vs-global point directly.

tree-bst-insertion-shapes.rationale: The guessing-game analogy in the search lesson already covers guesses stuck near one end; another would repeat it.

tree-rotations-avl-rule.rationale: Tiered group photo: left-to-right order = in-order, tiers = depth. Limit (middle subtree hand-over has no photo equivalent) correct.

tree-avl-height-bound.rationale: Counting argument; the table and Fibonacci growth explain it more directly than a comparison.

tree-avl-insertion-repair.rationale: Case table and traces; the rotation analogy is in the preceding lesson.

tree-red-black-invariants.rationale: Checkpoints and rest stops: black nodes / no red-red. Verifier corrected the bound to stops (nodes) rather than distance and retitled it to avoid the road-network-routing link. Limit (rebalancing needed; ratio vs logarithmic height) correct.

tree-red-black-insertion.rationale: Procedural repair outline; the 2-3-4-tree note already supplies the structural model.

tree-balanced-workloads.rationale: Decision/comparison of real systems; an analogy would not add understanding.

tree-heap-order-layout.rationale: Chain of command = heap order on each downward chain, siblings and cousins unordered. Verifier fixed the 'junior outranks senior' contradiction. Limit (heaps reshuffle and stay complete) correct.

tree-heap-sifting.rationale: Procedural sift operations; heap-order analogy precedes.

tree-bottom-up-heapify.rationale: The counting picture explains the linear bound more directly than a comparison.

tree-python-top-k.rationale: Venue door policy: min-heap root = weakest guest, x > h[0] = door check, heapreplace = swap. Limit (log₂ k repair swaps) correct.

tree-heap-merging.rationale: Sorted post piles: visible tops = heap of heads. Verifier changed 'about ten comparisons' to 'about ten levels'. Limit (many piles need the heap) correct.

tree-trie-lookup-prefixes.rationale: Lettered signposts: junction = node, turning = edge, plaque = end flag. Limit (per-node slot memory) correct; 'road network' reworded.

tree-trie-autocomplete.rationale: Builds directly on the signpost analogy; the code walk is the objective.

tree-trie-memory.rationale: 26 letter trays per desk = child-pointer array, mostly empty. Limit (slots cannot be shared; store only real children or compress) correct.

tree-radix-variants.rationale: Most specific delivery rule = longest prefix match. Limit (routers match bits from the most significant bit at line rate) correct.

tree-lca-single-query.rationale: Smallest area containing two addresses = LCA. Verifier fixed the limit's description of the general algorithm (it searches downward).

tree-lca-preprocessing.rationale: Express lifts 1, 2, 4, 8, 16 floors = binary-lifting levels; 13 = 8 + 4 + 1. Limit (per-node tables, memory, rebuild) correct.

tree-diameter-postorder.rationale: Longest walk on a loop-free trail system bending at a junction = diameter. Limit (real trails loop; trees have one path per pair) correct.

tree-downward-path-sums.rationale: Odometer readings: segment = difference of readings, crossing off abandoned branch = backtrack. Limit (negative values, counts) correct.

tree-maximum-path-gain.rationale: Same 'return one, record another' shape as the diameter lesson, whose analogy covers it.

tree-null-serialisation.rationale: Dictating a seating plan with 'empty' for gaps = null markers in pre-order. Verifier moved two technical sentences out of the collapsed limit; limit (fixed theatre grid vs unknown tree shape) correct.

tree-traversal-reconstruction.rationale: Procedure built on traversal orders; an analogy would not add understanding.
